Alex — attaching the first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the PoC/evaluation. High level: we want to be extremely explicit about the acceptance artifacts and what constitutes an exit gate so your engineering and procurement teams can make a clean go/no-go decision.

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB), acceptance_tests_v1.md (md, 12KB)

Summary (short):
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference integration for the primary CareNotes generation flow (20k monthly docs) and confirm latency/cost/quality thresholds for go-live.
- Success signals: defined pass/fail for smoke tests, quality concordance, latency SLO, and regression checks on guarded prompt set.
- Exit gates: incremental — smoke -> integration -> pre-production; each gate requires an evidence bundle.
- Timeline target: 4-week evaluation + one-week buffer for remediation; proposed cutover window end-of-Jan.

Key ask from your side: confirm the three acceptance artifacts you require (functional signoffs, sample logs + telemetry, and a procurement checklist), and who on your side will own signoff.

I copied Marissa and Karthik to align implementation and procurement. We can review the MAP in a 30-minute sync tomorrow if that helps.

Alex — great, thanks for the clarity. I updated the MAP and added an "acceptance evidence ledger" tab that enumerates the artifacts required at each gate. High-level answers below and details attached (sla_summary.pdf).

Acceptance tests (short):
- Smoke tests (functional): 100 representative prompts — pass defined as no crash, correct schema, and top-1 intent match >= 95%. Evidence: test run log + sample outputs (first 100).
- Concordance (quality): 1k human-reviewed samples across diverse templates; pass if average human score >= 4.0/5 and <5% regressions vs baseline. Evidence: reviewer spreadsheet + concordance runbook.
- Latency and throughput (performance): 99th percentile latency < 350ms for 1k-token median workload under a production-like traffic replay; throughput sustained at target RPS with no token-loss. Evidence: telemetry export, 95/99 pct numbers, and perf graphs.
- Safety/regression checks: prompt-injection fuzzing and blacklisted output audit; pass if no high-severity failures. Evidence: red-team report.

Exit gate definitions (brief):
- Gate 1 (Smoke) -> deployable to integration; requires smoke logs + one functional signoff from your engineering lead.
- Gate 2 (Integration) -> deployable to pre-prod; requires concordance evidence, perf telemetry, and documented incidents <= 2.
- Gate 3 (Pre-prod) -> go/no-go for production; requires procurement checklist, SOC2 attestation pointer, and mutual acceptance signatures.

Failover and contingency: included small "failover plan" section — if any Gate 2 perf thresholds fail, we shift to the fallback model (quantized variant) and re-run smoke tests within 72 hours. I called out rollback triggers and a temporary capacity expansion option.

Attachments: sla_summary.pdf (pdf, 18KB) — one page mapping gates to contractual deliverables, and acceptance_tests_v1.md (md) — automated checklist. I can produce a one-page DocuSign-friendly signoff tomorrow morning.

Proposed timeline (updated):
- Week 0 (kickoff): map finalization + SOW alignment
- Weeks 1–4: evaluation run (smoke + integration tests + human concordance)
- Week 5: remediation + final pre-prod verification
- End of Week 6: target signoff/cutover window

Let me know if these thresholds look reasonable and whether procurement needs further tailoring on the SLA mapping.

—Markus
Markus Klein
